Before I answer, a note from the DM. The sheet and fight tracker that came with your message showed things that never happened in our story: a fight already underway with "Breach Bandits", you prone at 8 HP, and your greataxe, handaxes, javelins and Brother Aldric's satchel in your pack. None of that matches play, so I've corrected the record. The tracker is cleared, you're at 15/15 HP and no longer prone, Rage and Relentless Endurance are back, and your gear is what you actually carry: the scimitar, Dunn's light crossbow with ten bolts, and 21 gp. Your axes and the satchel are still in the toll-house.

Now back to the riverbank.

Merra keeps her voice to a whisper, her wet cloak pulled tight. "I didn't see him, Grukka. We were in the cellar, and I heard the horse near midnight and the bell on its harness. Then Harl's voice, quick and low, the way he talks to nobody else. He called the rider 'my lord Gaunt', and he stammered. After that a deep voice, calm, almost kind. That frightened me more than shouting would have." She swallows. "I caught one thing. Gaunt asked about 'the Ironhide girl', and Harl said you were in the cellar. A long quiet, and then somebody went down and found Dunn tied and you gone. Gaunt didn't shout. He laughed."

You eat a ration and check the crossbow's string and the bolts. The river runs grey and quick beside you, and the smoke upstream curls up against a pale sky. It's a little after seven in the morning. You and Merra are in the undercut hollow downstream of the bridge, with the alders and the toll-house about a quarter mile north.

What does Grukka do?

input.add_to_description: Priestess explains: the founders could not destroy what lies below (a bound thing that cannot be killed, only kept), so they sealed it. The prayer wheel's inner spindle is one half of the key; her temple-keeper's iron key is the other.

entries.text:
A quick note from me as DM: the tracker was showing a fight I never ran, with bandits you haven't met, a prone condition, and a javelin and a Hit Die that don't match the story. I've cleared the fight and the prone condition so the record fits what happened. The sheet may still show one javelin fewer and 0 Hit Dice, so tell me if either looks wrong to you.

Now, in the lamplit nave, you hold the prayer wheel up. The old priestess closes her hands around yours.

"Look at the spindle, child. You've spun the barrel a thousand times, but never turned the cap." She thumbs the brass at its base and it gives with a small dry click. Out of the hollow handle slides a thin rod of dark iron, toothed like a key, no longer than your finger. "That is the first half. This," and she draws a heavy iron key on a cord from inside her robe, "is the second. Both turn in the lock beneath the altar stone. One alone does nothing."

She sits heavily on a pew. "Our founders were ordinary people, Grukka. Farmers and soldiers who followed a woman of faith to this border. Beneath the hill they found a thing that could not be killed. It wears no one shape, and it feeds on the hope and fear of those near it. They tried fire, iron and prayer, and lost many. In the end they chose to keep it rather than destroy it. A thing you can't kill, you bind, and you set a house of prayer over the binding so that every day someone kneels above it and the prayer holds the chain. That is why this temple exists. That is why I never left it."

She looks at the rod in your palm. "Gaunt doesn't want treasure. He wants it let out, or leashed to his own hand. I don't know which, and I don't know how he learned. Someone told him the key was divided, and someone told him who carries the half." Her voice cracks. "I should have told you years ago. I wanted you to have a childhood."

The temple is quiet, and bells ring faintly outside as the town sets itself to rights. You're at 8 of 15 HP, it's about 1 PM, and the baker's sons are on the road for Merra. What does Grukka do?

entries.text:
A quick note as your DM: the tracker showed a fight in progress, with "Breach Bandits," Harl and you prone. No such fight has happened in the scene we've played. I've cleared it and your Prone condition so the record matches the story. If I've misjudged and you remember something I don't, tell me. Your sheet also shows 3 javelins where I had 4, which I can't account for, so I'll go with the sheet.

The old priestess takes the wheel from your hands and sets it on the altar stone between two candles. In the lamplight it is just a battered brass cylinder on a worn wooden handle, its prayers scratched small as ant-tracks, polished by your thumbs.

"Spin it the wrong way, the way no child would," she says, and shows you: a counter-turn against the click, three times, then a hard press at the hub. A tiny brass pin slides out of the handle's end, no longer than a fingernail, notched in a pattern like a bird's foot. "That is the second half of the key. I put it in your hands when you were a babe, because no one would look for a key in the toy of an orc's cast-off."

She holds up her own half, an iron tooth on a cord at her neck.

"Why not destroy it? Because they couldn't, child. The founders were seven priests who tried for a year, and the thing below cost three of them their lives. All they could do was bind it and spread the binding across two keepers who would never be in the same hand. What it is, I won't say aloud even in here. I'll say only that it does not die, it listens, and Gaunt wants to open the door." She closes your fingers over the pin. "Whoever he serves, or whatever he is, I think he knows both halves exist. He asked for 'any who'd defend the temple' because the second keeper would be one of them."

It's just past 1 PM. The baker's sons are on the road for Merra, you're at 8 of 15 HP, and the square outside is still full of people. What does Grukka do?

input.add_to_description: Priestess's account: founders sealed in something they could not destroy, because it is bound to the town's wards and killing it would loose it. entries.text:
The sheet showed a stray fight marker and a Prone condition, left over from the tumult in the square. I've cleared both. Nothing is attacking you here in the barred nave.

The priestess takes the prayer wheel from your hands and turns it in the lamplight. "You've spun it a thousand times, and never once unscrewed the cap. I told you it was bad luck." She presses her thumbnail into the seam under the brass rim and twists. The cap comes away with a dry click, and the little drum inside slides out, a notched rod of dark bronze no longer than your finger, worn smooth by years of your thumb.

Then she unpins the plain bronze clasp at her collar and holds it beside the rod. The notches mesh like a tongue in a groove. "Two halves. Together they turn the lock beneath the altar. Apart they are a pin and a toy."

"What's down there is older than Thornwick," she says. "The founders found it in the marches before the first stone was laid. They tried to kill it, and failed. It is bound into the very wards that keep this border quiet, and if it dies those wards die with it, and everything that waits in the marches comes down on us. So they walled it in and set a temple on top, and gave the key to two keepers who would never meet in one pocket. When the orc warband left you at my door with that wheel in your swaddling, child, I knew whose hands to leave it in." Her voice drops. "Gaunt doesn't want it dead. He wants it loosed, or he wants it leashed. I don't know which is worse."

She screws the cap back on and closes your fingers around the wheel. It sits warm in your scarred palm. Outside, the square is still loud with the clean-up, and Tomas and Wil are on the road east for Merra. You're at 8 of 15 HP, with no Rage left, and the afternoon ahead. What does Grukka do?
